And, O friend, for those purified in body, speech, mind, and phenomena, the protectors of the enclosure—consisting of the six classes [of deities] whose nature is the ten directional guardians, planets, nāgas, and spirits, appearing in the forms of wrathful kings born from the six elements of gnosis, space, wind, fire, water, and earth, and residing within the gabled pavilion with its three or five enclosures—should be assigned internally and externally through the yoga of union (*saṃpuṭayoga*). [The numerical sequence: 15, 20, 25, 25, 50, 26. *Vimalaprabhā*, [Section on Initiation].

Those arisen from the elements of earth and water are the protectors of the body-element; those arisen from the elements of fire and wind are the protectors of the speech-element; and those arisen from the elements of space and gnosis are the protectors of the mind-element everywhere.
This is the rule of the Blessed One;
therefore, whatever is desired by practitioners must be accomplished in accordance with the guru’s rules—this is the rule. || 23 ||

Having perceived from afar the three enclosures situated within the three circles of the earth, at the conclusion of the morning when the shadows have vanished, the yogi should visualize himself—free from all impurity—upon the summit of that diamond-peak in the sky: with a lotus in the center, a sun in the middle, a hand-sized pericarp, and a throne extending for four cubits. ||24||
Now, for each of these—anger and the others—there are mantra-syllables for the bali offering.

Namely: *Oṃ āḥ hūṃ hoḥ*. To Uṣṇīṣa, Sumbhani, Sumbhavighnāntaka, Nīladaṇḍa, Prajñāntaka, Yamāntaka, Padmāntaka, Acala, Yamāntaka, Mahābala, and their retinues, we offer this *bali*, perfume, flower, incense, lamp, and unbroken grain. May they come with their retinues and quickly accept, eat, and drink this *bali*: *jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ*. Being fully satisfied, may they perform peace, nourishment, protection, defense, and concealment for all sentient beings: *huṃ hūṃ phaṭ*. Vajradhara commands: *svāhā*. This is the mantra for the *bali* offering to all the wrathful deities (*krodha*).

Likewise, the mantra-words for the bali offering to those who have accomplished the totalities (*kṛtsna*) beginning with space: *Oṃ āḥ hūṃ hoḥ! To those who have mastered space, wind, fire, water, and earth, together with their retinues, we offer this bali, fragrance, flowers, incense, lamp, and unbroken grain.

Having arrived, may you and your retinues quickly accept, eat, and drink this bali! Jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ! Being fully satisfied, may you grant peace, nourishment, protection, shelter, and guardianship to all sentient beings! Huṃ hūṃ phaṭ! Vajradhara commands: svāhā!*

Then, the mantra-words for the offering (*bali*) to the guardians of the directions (*dikpāla*): *oṃ āḥ hūṃ hoḥ*. To Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Nairṛti, Vāyu, Yama, Agni, Samudra, Īśvara, Indra, and Yakṣa, together with their retinues, we offer this *bali*, perfume, flowers, incense, lamp, and unbroken grain. May they come with their retinues and quickly accept, eat, and drink this *bali*: *jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ*. Being fully satisfied, may they provide peace, nourishment, protection, defense, and concealment for all sentient beings: *huṃ hūṃ phaṭ*. Vajradhara commands this; *svāhā*.

Then, the mantra syllables for the offering to the planets (*graha-bali*): Oṃ āḥ hūṃ ho! To Rāhu, Kālāgni, Candra, Sūrya, Budha, Maṅgala, Śukra, Bṛhaspati, Ketu, and Śani, together with their retinues, we offer this *bali*, fragrance, flowers, incense, lamp, and unbroken rice grains. May they come with their retinues and quickly accept, eat, and drink this *bali*: Jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ! Being fully satisfied, may they grant peace, nourishment, protection, defense, and concealment to all sentient beings: Huṃ hūṃ phaṭ! Vajradhara commands it: Svāhā!

Then, the mantra-words for the *nāga* offering: Oṃ āḥ hūṃ hoḥ! To Jaya, Vijaya, Padma, Karkoṭaka, Vāsuki, Śaṅkhapāla, Kulika, Ananta, Takṣaka, Mahāpadma, and their retinues, we offer this *bali*, scent, flower, incense, lamp, and unbroken grain. May they come with their retinues and quickly accept, eat, and drink this *bali*: jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ! Being fully satisfied, may they provide peace, nourishment, protection, defense, and concealment for all sentient beings! Huṃ hūṃ phaṭ! Vajradhara commands: svāhā!

Then, the mantra-syllables for the *bali* offering to the spirits (*bhūta*): *oṃ āḥ haiṃ hoḥ*, we offer this *bali*, fragrance, flower, incense, lamp, and unbroken grain to the Vetālas with their transformed faces, to those with the faces of dogs, crows, pigs, vultures, tigers, owls, jackals, and Garuḍas, together with their retinues. May they come with their retinues and quickly accept, eat, and drink this: *jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ*. Being fully satisfied, may they provide peace, nourishment, protection, defense, and concealment for all sentient beings: *huṃ hūṃ phaṭ*. Vajradhara commands this: *svāhā*. This is the *bhūtabali* mantra.

Having thus purified, awakened, ignited, and transformed into nectar the individual offerings (*pratyekabali*) according to the sequence to be described, the mantra-practitioner offers them to the wrathful deities (*krodha*) and so forth.
Having likewise offered the four twilight offerings (*catuḥ-sandhyā-bali*) throughout the entire mandala ritual, the preceptor then performs the dismissal (*visarjana*).
At the time of dismissal, he should cause the circle of wrathful deities (*krodhacakra*) to enter the syllable *UṂ* within the secret wheel (*guhyacakra*).

One should cause the wheel of the totality of emptiness (*śūnyakṛtsna*) and so forth to enter the syllable *Aṃ* at the crown of the head; the wheel of the guardians of the directions (*dikpāla*) into the syllable *Ai* at the forehead; the wheel of the planets (*graha*) into the syllable *Ṛ* at the throat; the wheel of the nāgas (*nāga*) into the syllable *Au* at the heart; and the wheel of the spirits (*bhūta*) into the syllable *Ṛ* at the navel. Having thus completed the procedure for dismissal (*visarjana*), the mantra-practitioner then performs the ritual appropriation of the site (*bhūmiparigraha*) according to the sequence to be described; such is the rule. (24)

Now, the invocation of the Earth is described for the purpose of purifying the ground through the meditative absorption (samādhi) to be explained: Having first offered the *bali* oblation to the Kṣetrapāla three times on the ground in all directions, one should subsequently burn away the host of Māras situated in the four cardinal and intermediate directions with the [mantra] *vaḥ*.
Then, having invoked the Earth and offered an *argha* of water and flowers to her, one should indeed request her, saying: "O Dwellress of the Earth, perform purification as you desire. ||25||

Here, having summoned the Earth with the *pṛthvī-samādhi* mantra, and having offered the *argha* to her using the previously mentioned *argha*-vessel containing water, flowers, and fragrant substances along with these mantra-words—*jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ*—one should then pray to her, saying "Perform purification as you desire in this dwelling on earth"; this is the subsequent prayer (*anuprārthanā*). || 25 ||

O Goddess, you were the witness to the Victor’s defeat of Māra when he was accompanied by the Lord of the Gods; therefore, O you who are saluted by the best of deities, you are worthy of worship. Accept, accept this half [of the water] from me, just as the Victor destroyed even the powerful army of Māra for the sake of awakening, so too do I destroy Māra for the sake of my disciples’ consecration. 26.

"O Goddess Vimalaprabhā, you who were present as a witness when the Lord of the Gods joined forces with the Jina to shatter Māra; therefore, O you who are saluted by the best of gods, you are worthy of worship. Accept, accept this water-offering from me! Having thus praised her, he should entreat her:

"Just as the Jina shattered even the powerful army of Māra for the sake of awakening, so too shall I destroy Māra for the sake of conferring initiation upon my disciples, with you acting as my witness.
Then, having performed the worship of the Buddhas and others as will be described, and having offered the water-offering (argha) and so forth, he should entreat them. (26)

Here is the prayer: "May those Buddhas in all directions, who are free from defilement, and the Bodhisattvas together with their consorts, protect me indeed with supreme compassion for the sake of initiation (*sekha*) in the mandala.

Having thus supplicated them all, one should nail the ground with stakes made of hard khadira wood. One should then place the directional Wrathful Deities (*dikkrodha*), equipped with their weapons, in their respective directions for the purpose of protection. ||27||

"May those Buddhas in all directions, free from defilement, along with the Bodhisattvas and their consorts, protect me indeed with supreme compassion for the sake of the consecration in the maṇḍala. Having thus supplicated them all, one should nail the ground with stakes made of firm khadira wood according to the sequence to be described; such is the rule for the supplication.
Likewise, one should place the aforementioned wrathful deities in the ten directions together with their weapons for the purpose of nailing the earth and protecting it; such is the rule. || 27 ||

Now, the signs regarding the excavation of the ground are described: if a thorn, charcoal, or a horn—which causes fear of death—is found embedded within the earth at that spot, destruction occurs; therefore, it must be cleared away according to its nature.

For gems, conch shells, and glass produce sensory pleasure; thus, for the sake of a mandala, a palace, a house, or for the purpose of performing sacrifices and so forth, the ground is prepared with these fixed requirements.
In this case, if a thorn or similar object is embedded within the ground, it creates an obstacle for virtuous activity;

therefore, the thorn must be cleared away. Whether it be human bone, charcoal with its embers, or something common like a horn, it causes fear of death; in that place, during such virtuous activity, ruin occurs. For that reason, by virtue of its qualities, it must indeed be removed. Furthermore, if a jewel, a conch, or glass is seen, then it brings happiness for the purpose of the mandala on the ground.
Likewise, for the sake of a palace, a house, or for the purpose of sacrifices and the like manifested here, there is the rule regarding the purification of the site. || 28 ||

[Excavation, the horn with charcoal in the chapter, verses 29–30. The Great Chapter on the Collection of the Ground and Other Elements Preceded by the Protection Circle: Now, the day for the purification of the ground is stated— On the full moon day (Pūrṇā) there is the purification of the ground, as well as the eclipse and the initiation of the "sons" (putrakas). On the twelfth day (Dvādaśī), the laying of the thread; on the day of Madana, the falling of the venerable powder (śrī-rajas).

On the full moon day, the excellent Guru bestows the consecration (seka) and so forth. And on that day of the destruction of Māra, the installation (pratiṣṭhā) takes place at night; in the family of the Jinas, the installation occurs at night, not at any other time of night. || 29 ||
Regarding the passage beginning with "In the full [moon]," etc.:
here, in every month there are six full [moon] days, namely—two fifth days, two tenth days, and two fifteenth days.

Having determined the time limit for drawing the mandala and having ascertained whether the karma is auspicious or inauspicious, one should purify the ground on an auspicious occasion, such as the fifth, tenth, or fifteenth of the bright fortnight, avoiding the *viṣṭi* lunar day.
Then, one should fill [the pit] with the previously mentioned earth;

thus, for an inauspicious rite, one should purify the ground on the fifth or tenth day of the dark fortnight, or on the new moon when the moon has disappeared, and fill it with the aforementioned earth. Furthermore, regarding the eclipse [rite], one should perform worship and so forth on the full moon.
The gathering of the spiritual sons and disciples takes place on the full moon day.
Then, having ascertained the time for drawing the mandala, the laying of the thread (sūtrapāta) should be performed on the twelfth day;
on the thirteenth day, which is the day of Madana, and on the fourteenth day, the falling of the venerable powder (śrīrajaḥpāta) should be performed.
The scriptural reading states that the master bestows the initiation and so forth to be described on the full moon day; however,
the rule is that the excellent master bestows it on the day of the destruction of Māra (the eighth day), and by virtue of the word "and" (*ca*), also on the other full moon day.

Thus, the consecration of images and the like takes place on that very night of the full moon; there is no consecration on any other night within the lineage of the Jinas—such is the rule regarding the lunar day (tithi). || 29 ||

O Lord of Men, for others, the consecration (pratiṣṭhā) takes place at night when the ascendant is pure and the planets are favorable; however, if Jupiter and Venus have set, then indeed no marriage or consecration should take place.
Having understood all this—both worldly and transcendental—the preceptor performs whatever task he undertakes within the abode of the earth, and all that becomes auspicious and effective. ||30||
Furthermore, O Lord of Men, regarding the night-time installation: when the planets and so forth are situated in a pure *lagna*,
and Jupiter (*bṛhaspati*) and Venus (*śukra*) have set, having entered the solar disc— if that occurs,
then in that month there is absolutely no marriage or installation.

Thus, when the sun has entered the domain of Jupiter (the sign of Taurus), on the full moon day of Puṣya or Caitra, there occurs again the "Puṣya-consecration" for a king; this is the rule that on Caitra there is the "Buddha-consecration. Having understood this, whatever ritual the Master performs in this entire abode of the earth—whether mundane or supramundane, such as rites for pacification and so forth—all that becomes effective and fruit-bearing. Such is the rule regarding the lunar days (tithi).
Likewise, this is the rule for cruel rites and inauspicious days. || 30 ||

Now, the procedure for protecting the disciple is stated: Having performed the consecration, one should perform the protection of the disciple at the head, the heart, as well as the crown-protrusion (*uṣṇīṣa*), the navel, and the throat, with the Victors and so forth belonging to both families, [protecting] body, speech, and mind.

Thus, for the sake of the liberation of beings—whether they be clay [images] and the like, or books—with the glorious vowels clearly and fixedly assigned, O Lord, I cause even this mandala to be drawn. (31)

In this context, having first performed protection for the disciple and others, one should subsequently accept the disciple and so forth. Here, according to the Jinas and other deities belonging to both families, protection is established on the head with the syllable *ū*, on the heart with *ī*, on the crown (*uṣṇīṣa*) with *ā*, at the navel with *l*, on the throat with *ṛ*, and in the secret place with *ā*—
these being the deities belonging to both families, distinguished as body, speech, and mind.
Thus, for the *lepā* and so forth, by means of the five vowels clearly established as fixed— the venerable vowels *ai*, *ṛ*, *u*, *lṛ*, and *ū*.

"Having performed the protection of the books, one should then supplicate the Buddhas for the sake of the liberation of sentient beings, saying: 'I am having this mandala of the Blessed Kālacakra drawn;
therefore, may the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas bestow their blessing upon the disciples and others. This is the rule for the supplication and the rule for the protection. || 31 ||

Now, it is said in brief: In a pure place, well-filled, beautifully arranged, and elevated like the back of a tortoise, measuring one to ten cubits—or even a thousand years of a noble king’s reign—having placed the thread, the vajra, and the colored powders in the directions of Indra, Yama, Varuṇa, and the North, and having offered the vajra-bell, when the auspicious sign is obtained, the mandala should be laid out with the thread on the first or the subsequent day. ||32||
In that regard, since the consecration (*adhivāsana*) of the sūtras and so forth will be explained in detail below,

[one should perform it] in a pure place that is well-filled, beautifully arranged, square, and slightly elevated like the back of a tortoise; in a space measuring one cubit and so on— namely four cubits, eight cubits, sixteen cubits, and likewise up to a measurement of one thousand cubits— which is complete.

In that regard, having placed the thread in the east, the vajra in the south, the pigments and vessels in the west, the vajra-bell in the north, and the *vijaya* flask in the center, then, according to the sequence to be described, when the master or the disciple obtains a sign while asleep, then—once the sign has been obtained—the mandala must first be laid out toward the eastern direction and subsequently toward the western direction by the teacher and the disciple; such is the rule. ||32||
And with the goddesses,
by means of the five Śrī-sounds; that is, by means of the five sounds of the books.

For the sake of brevity for the disciples, there is no [separate] "Great Chapter" (*mahoddeśa*) on the summary of the preliminary stages such as the protection wheel (*rakṣācakra*) and so forth. Now, the characteristics of ill omens are stated: If the cord is broken, there is injury to the Guru; likewise, if the *parigha* (astronomical obstacle) is transgressed, there is injury to the "sons" (disciples). If dust is stirred up by the wind, it reveals danger and the collapse of the kingdom within the realm.

Having seen that ill omen, the Lord should again perform the recitation of mantras; once the omen has been obtained once more, the laying out of the lines (sūtrapāta) should be performed with even and uneven steps. || 33 ||
In this case, if the thread is severed, harm comes to the preceptor;
furthermore, if the cross-bar is transgressed while the dust is stirred up by the wind, harm comes to the disciples.
In this regard, it is the rule that when dust is raised by a whirlwind (*maṇḍalika-vāta*), it reveals fear for the teacher and others, and it reveals the collapse of the king within the kingdom.
Having seen such an ill omen, the preceptor should again perform the recitation of the *vibhoma-mantra* until the omen occurs once more.
Then, once the sign has been further obtained, the laying of the lines (*sūtrapāta*) must be performed with both even and uneven steps.

Here, the rule is that the laying of the lines is to be performed by the teacher with the left leg in the cross-legged posture (*paryaṅka*) and the sole of the right foot resting on the ground—this is done with an even step; and by the reverse, it is to be done with an uneven step. Thus is the rule. || 33 ||

Now the *parigha* (obstacle) is described: Within the limbs of wisdom and method, the *parigha* occurs in the mandala and must be avoided on the ground. At the time of battle, when it has reached the fire and wind [houses], it is like a serpent in the midst of the army;

there is destruction of the army on the surface of the earth. However, in a battle of limbs, it is a blow. Therefore, in battle and in consecration (*seka*), the mantra-practitioner should recognize the exceedingly powerful *parigha*. (34)
In this context, among the components of wisdom (*prajñā*) and means (*upāya*), the crossbar (*parigha*) arises; it must be avoided in the mandala.
Here, the component of wisdom is the south-west, and the component of means is the north-east;
between these two, the crossbar must be avoided in the mandala.

Thus, on the ground at the time of battle, when it is said that [the breath] has gone to the fire and wind [elements], meaning when the two armies have advanced as far as the southeast and northwest directions, then like a serpent in the midst of them, taking the form of a staff in the battle,
there occurs the destruction of the army due to the leaping over the *parigha* (obstructive line) upon the surface of the earth.
In a limb-to-limb combat there is a blow; in a circular formation there is strife and conflict.
Therefore, in battle and in the consecration (seka), the minister must understand the exceedingly powerful iron club (parigha); such is the rule. || 34 ||

Now, the visualization of the chosen deity (iṣṭadevatā) is briefly described: Having meditated upon the syllables beginning with *ā* and *ka* within the lotus of one’s own heart, atop the moon, sun, and fire, one should contemplate the glorious Kālacakra, who stands in the *ālīḍha* posture, trampling the Moon and Madana, appearing terrifying and fierce. To his right is Vimalaprabhā; in the lotus of the heart of Wisdom (Prajñā), within the union of sun and moon, one should draw in the Buddhas by means of their respective vajra-hooks. Then the Goddesses, having attained a state of equal flavor (*samarasa*) within the dust, are to be visualized as being fixed upon the thread. || 35 ||
"By the first [vowels]" means by the vowels beginning with *ā*; "by the *ka*-group" means by the consonants beginning with *ka*, which consist of the moon and sun;
"together with the *savarna*" means accompanied by the syllable *hūṃ*.

Having meditated upon the venerable Kālacakra—trampled by the moon and Madana, standing in the *ālīḍha* posture—upon the lotus of his own heart above the moon, sun, and fire according to the sequence to be described, one should summon the Buddhas with their respective vajra-hooks from the lotus of the heart of the Wisdom Consort (Prajñā) within the enclosure of the sun and moon, [saying] "O Goddess! (*devī*).
The rule is that on the colored powder (*rajas*), the Buddhas are to be visualized in the form of the powder, and on the laid-out lines, the goddesses are to be visualized in the form of the lines.
Now, beginning from the invocation of the previous ground (*pūrvabhūmi*) up until this meditative absorption (*samādhi*), the ritual procedure of the mantra is stated;
it is described as the deity-absorption, the subjugation of Māra, the mantra, the placement of the limbs (*aṅganyāsa*) of the Blessed One Kālacakra, and the purification of body, speech, and mind.

Here, first, in the *Sādhanāpaṭala*, according to the sequence to be explained, one should perform the purification of the face, the worship of the Tathāgatas, the confession of sins, the rejoicing in merit, the going for refuge in the Three Jewels, the offering of one’s own body, the generation of the thought of awakening (*bodhicitta*), and the taking of recourse to the path; thereafter, having taken emptiness as the object of focus, there are the mantra-words that purify the body, speech, mind, and gnosis for the purpose of accomplishing the deity.

Reciting this mantra— *oṃ āḥ hūṃ ho haṃ kṣaḥ prajñopāyātmakakāyavākcittajñānādhipate mama kāyavākcittajñānavajraṃ vajrāmṛtasvabhāvaṃ kuru kuru skandhadhātvāyatanaṃ niḥsvabhāva svāhā*— the practitioner should meditate upon a vajra-moon mandala, complete with its sixteen digits, transformed from the syllable *vaṃ* above the crown of the head (*uṣṇīṣa*).
Then, starting from the turban and down to the tips of the toenails, one should discard one's own body three times like a snake shedding its skin;

thereafter, one should meditate on oneself as having the form of the moon. For pacification and nourishment, as well as for subjugation and attraction, one should meditate on it as red-colored with the solar disc. Likewise, for killing and expulsion, [one should meditate] with the transformation of the syllable *repha* (ra), and for [subjugation], with the transformation of the syllable *yaṃ* as the black lunar disc of Rāhu.

For the rites of immobilization (stambhana) and delusion (mohana), the practitioner should meditate on himself as yellow, with a yellow tail, and a yellow lunar disc, [all] transformed from the syllable *laṃ*;

for the rite of revivification (pratyujjīvana), he should meditate on himself as green, with a universal color (viśvavarṇa), and a green celestial disc (ākāśamaṇḍala) transformed from the syllable *haṃ*.
Then, he should utter this mantra:

Having recited: *Oṃ, all phenomena are pure by nature; I am pure by nature*, one should then place: white Amitābha at the forehead; red Ratnasaṃbhava at the throat with *Āḥ*; black Amoghasiddhi at the heart with *Hūṃ*; yellow Vairocana at the navel with *Hoḥ*; dark-green Akṣobhya on the crown of the head (*uṣṇīṣa*) with *Haṃ*; and blue Vajrasattva at the secret place with *Kṣaḥ*. These should be visualized as bearing the colors, weapons, and implements of the arms that will be described hereafter. This is the rule for the ritual of the placement of the six families (*ṣaṭkulanyāsa*), which constitutes the purification of the vajra-face. Now, the mantra for the placement of the purification of the hands is stated:
Oṃ haḥ! O King of all weapons, who brings an end to Māra and the afflictions, O Vajra-sharp one, who cuts through suffering, purify my hands! Svāhā!

With this mantra, having performed the mutual clasping of hands, one should rub [them] with the syllable *Ram*, presided over by the maṇḍala of Rāhu, preceded by the protection wheel (*rakṣācakra*), and so forth. This is the mantra for washing the hands. *Vaṃ haḥ sarvāstrāntaka...* [This concludes] the Great Chapter on the Collection of the Ground and Other Elements, which serves as the introduction to the protection wheel.
Then, according to the previously mentioned sequence, the fifteen vowels from *a* to *l̥*— namely, *a, i, ṛ, u, l̥, a, e, ar, o, al, ha, ya, ra, va, la*—
should be placed upon the finger-joint nodes of the left hand, beginning with the root node of the little finger (*kaniṣṭhā*).
On the right hand, starting from the upper joint of the thumb and proceeding up to the third joint below the little finger, the letters beginning with *lā* should be assigned—namely:
*lā vā rā yā hā ālū au ār ai ā lū ū ṛ ī ā*—in the sequence of earth and the other elements.

Then, having visualized a blue-syllable *hūṃ* in the center of the moon and sun within the hollowed palms, one should then form the five-pronged vajra-mudrā described by those seed-syllables of the moon, sun, and Rāhu, as will be explained below.
With that [mantra], one should touch oneself starting from the crown of the head down to the nails of the toes;

then, one should recite this mantra: *oṃ ā hūṃ hoḥ haṃ kṣaḥ, O Sovereign of Body, Speech, Mind, and Gnosis, Vajra-body, make my body, speech, mind, and gnosis-vajra have the nature of the Vajra-body, make it so, svāhā!*
Then, for the purification of body, speech, mind, and gnosis, one performs the ego-identification with: *oṃ sarvatathāgatavajrakāyasvabhāvātmako’ham*.
Then, having performed the placement of the six families (*ṣaṭkulanyāsa*), one subsequently performs the placement of the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*).
Having formed a hollowed cavity with both hands, one places [the mantra] at the heart with the pair of thumbs: *oṃ hauṃ hṛdayāya namaḥ*.
On the head: Oṃ hūṃ, svāhā to the head. On the crest-lock: Oṃ haṝ, vauṣaṭ to the crest-lock.
On all limbs: Oṃ hrīṃ, huṃ to the armor.
One should touch all the limbs with both hands:
*oṃ hrāṃ netrāya vaṣaṭ* for the eyes;
*oṃ hrāḥ astrāya phaṭ* for the weapon-mantra.
In all directions, one should perform the placement of the weapon (*astra*) by snapping the forefinger and thumb—with the left hand for auspicious [rites] and the right for inauspicious ones.
Then, the procedure for the six-limbed placement (*ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*) is as follows: "Oṃ, I am of the nature of the vajra of the heart, head, crest, armor, eyes, and weapon of all Tathāgatas.

This six-limbed [placement] is further performed with earth and the other elements; moreover, according to another terminology of the twilight (*saṃdhyābhāṣā*), the heart is the navel, and likewise, the head is understood by its parts beginning with the heart, throat, forehead, and crown.

Then, one constructs the previously mentioned protection wheel (*rakṣācakra*) with this mantra: *oṃ āḥ hūṃ raḥ vajracandrasūryarāhukālāgnayaḥ kāyavākcittajñānavajraprākārān kuru kuru svāhā*. This is the mantra for the enclosure wall (*prākāra*). *oṃ hūṃ viśvakāya vajra vajrakūṭāgāraṃ kuru kuru svāhā*. This is the mantra for the peaked pavilion (*kūṭāgāra*).
*oṃ hāṃ yāṃ rāṃ vāṃ lāṃ vajrākāśavāyuteja udakapṛthivīvajrasvabhāvapañcadhātavo vajramaṇḍalāni kuru kuru svāhā*. This is the mantra for the placement of the lower mandalas (*adhomaṇḍalanyāsa*).
In the Upāyatantra, by means of these very [syllables], one constructs the peaked pavilion and so forth;
here, on the summit of Mount Meru, there is no mandala.
*Oṃ paṃ viśvavajrapadmaṃ kuru kuru svāhā*; this is the mantra of the lotus.
Oṃ raḥ vajrasūrya vajrasūryāsanaṃ kuru kuru svāhā—this is the mantra for the sun-seat.
Then, upon that, through devotion to the tantra, one should meditate on oneself as the Lord of Wrath (Krodhendra):
Oṃ hūṃ, I am Krodhendra, the giver of commands to the wrathful ones, svāhā.
Then, out of anger, one should issue commands with their respective mantra words:
*Oṃ haṃ vajrakrodharāja mahoṣṇīṣa, protect, protect the upper direction, svāhā!
Oṃ yaṃ vajrakrodharāja atibala sarvavighnāntaka, protect, protect the eastern direction, svāhā!*
Oṃ raṃ vajrakrodharāja jambhaka duṣṭaprajñāntaka, protect, protect the southern direction, svāhā!
Oṃ vaṃ vajrakrodharāja mānakavirāgapadmāntaka, protect, protect the northern direction, svāhā!
Oṃ laṃ vajrakrodharāja stambhaka yamāntaka, protect, protect the western direction, svāhā!
Then, by virtue of their nature, the long vowels are to be taken in the intermediate directions according to the sequence of withdrawal (*saṃhārakrama*):
*oṃ lāḥ vajrakrodharāja mahābala vāyavyāṃ diśi rakṣāṃ kuru kuru svāhā*;
*oṃ vāḥ vajrakrodharājācala īśānadiśi rakṣāṃ kuru kuru svāhā*.
Oṃ rāḥ, Vajrakrodharāja Ṭakkirāja, protect, protect in the southwestern direction, svāhā!
Oṃ yāḥ, Vajrakrodharāja Nīladaṇḍa, protect, protect in the southeastern direction, svāhā!
Oṃ hāḥ, Vajrakrodharāja Sumbha, protect, protect in the downward direction, svāhā!
In this way, the mantra-practitioner should meditate upon the Wrathful Kings by means of the ritual for accomplishment taught in the tantra.

Then, having uttered, "I am the very nature of the protection wheel of all the Tathāgatas," he should maintain the sense of ego-identity (*ahaṅkāra*). This is the rule for the protection wheel. Thereafter, within his own heart, there is a universal lotus (*viśvapadma*) transformed from the syllable *paṃ*. Upon that, in the pericarp, is a moon mandala transformed from the syllable *aṃ*. Above that, according to one's devotion to the deity, is the seed-syllable of gnosis (*jñānabīja*). From that vajra, like a vajra-sun, he should radiate rays of light that awaken all the Tathāgatas throughout the expanse of space.

Then, having turned them back and caused them to enter the seed-syllable of gnosis (*jñānabīja*) within one's own heart, one should emanate perfumes, garlands, and so forth for the purpose of worshipping the Buddhas who have been radiated out in the form of mandalas within the element of space. From their respective seed-syllables of gnosis:
*oṃ c ch j jh ña vajragandhe gandhārcanaṃ kuru kuru svāhā*;
*oṃ c ch j jh ña vajramāle vajramālārcanaṃ kuru kuru svāhā*.
Oṃ ṭ ṭh ḍ ḍh ṇa vajradhūpe, perform the offering of incense, perform it, svāhā! Oṃ ṭ ṭh ḍ ḍh ṇā vajrapradīpe, perform the offering of lamps, perform it, svāhā!
Oṃ p ph b bh ma vajrāmṛte, perform the worship and offering of the food-oblation, perform it, svāhā!
Oṃ p ph b bh mā vajrāmṛte, perform the worship with indestructible fruits, perform it, svāhā!
Oṃ t th d dh na vajralāsye, perform the worship with garments and ornaments, perform it, svāhā!
Oṃ t th d dh nā vajrahāsye, perform the worship with the bell and mirror, perform it, svāhā!
Oṃ k kh g gh ṅa vajravādye vādyapūjāṃ kuru kuru svāhā | Oṃ k kh g gh ṅā vajranṛtye nṛtyapūjāṃ kuru kuru svāhā | Oṃ s ṣ ś ṣ ka vajragīte gītapūjāṃ kuru kuru svāhā ||

"Oṃ sa pa pa śa kā vajrakāme, perform, perform the adamantine surata-worship for all the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, Krodhas, and so forth, svāhā! Having performed a mental worship with these words of the Goddess's mantra, one should likewise offer salutation and worship to the Buddhas and others. Then, according to the procedure taught in the Tantra, one should perform the sevenfold worship: the confession of misdeeds, rejoicing in merit, going for refuge to the Three Jewels, the offering of one's own body, and the generation of the thought of awakening (bodhicitta). This is the ritual for the sevenfold worship.

Then, the practitioner should perform the yoga of the drop (*binduyoga*), the subtle yoga (*sūkṣmayoga*), the supreme king of the mandala (*maṇḍalarājāgrī*), and the supreme king of activities (*karmarājāgrī*), which have emptiness as their object;
thereafter, by the power of devotion to the tantra, one should cultivate the divine pride (*ahaṅkāra*) of the chosen deity with the mantra:
*oṃ sarvatathāgatādhipati-vajrasattvo'haṃ durdāntadamaka hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā*.

With this, one should empower oneself; thus [ends] the great chapter on the preliminary collection of the ground and so forth for the protection wheel of the deity, in the [relevant] chapter, verse [number].
Regarding the rule of the ego-sense (*ahaṅkāra-niyama*): having generated the ego-sense of the deity, one should then perform the appropriation of the site and the gathering of disciples.

First, having purified [the area], one should offer a bali-oblation to the lords of the region, village, and field with these mantra-words: Oṃ oṃ vajracandra sarvadharmasuviśuddhasvabhāva sarvadharmān viśodhaya svāhā. Oṃ āḥ vajrasūrya sarvadharmaprabodhaka sarvadharmān prabodhaya svāhā. Oṃ hūṃ vajrānala sarvadharmapradīpaka sarvadharmān pradīpaya svāhā. Oṃ hoḥ sarvadharmavajrāmṛtakara sarvadharmān vajrāmṛtaṃ kuru kuru svāhā.
With these mantra-words, one should purify with the left hand in the proper sequence,
awaken with the right hand by touching [the object], and then kindle it by covering it with joined palms (*añjali*).
Having prepared the vajra-nectar with the Vajragaruḍa mudrā, one should perform the invocation of the local ruler with the Trailokyavijaya mudrā.

Having performed the invocation with the dog-seal for the lords of village sites; with the five-pronged seal for the wrathful kings; with the knife-seal for all [spirits]; with the sword-seal for the deities; with the jewel-seal for the planetary spirits; with the lotus-seal for the nāgas; and with the wheel-seal for the pretas—[one should recite]: "Then, Oṃ Āḥ Hūṃ! [Name], come, come quickly! Take this offering, take it! Having eaten and drunk, having become satisfied, having generated a mind of peace toward all sentient beings, go, go to another place, svāhā!"
At the time of taking possession of the ground, one should say, "Go to your own place at another time.
In this manner, one should dispatch all the individual offerings (*bali*) according to the previously mentioned procedure for the division of directions; such is the ritual for the *bali*.
Then, one should meditate on a yellow wheel transformed from the syllable *lāṃ* upon the moon-maṇḍala in one's own heart.

One should meditate upon the earth transformed from that [syllable] as having three faces and six arms, holding a wheel, a staff, and a vajra in her right hands, and holding a conch, a chain, and a vajra-bell in her left hands; she is yellow in color, wears yellow garments, and is adorned with yellow jewel ornaments. Then, having unified the commitment-being (*samayasattva*) with the wisdom-being (*jñānasattva*), one should invoke the external goddess of the earth according to the sequence to be described by means of this mantra: *oṃ lāṃ āḥ vasundhare sarvabuddhajanani sarvasattvopakāriṇi vajrasattva ājñāpayati śīghramāgaccha āgaccha idam*.

"I offer you fragrance, flowers, incense, lamps, food offerings, fruits, and unbroken rice; please accept them, accept them for the sake of the maṇḍala. Grant me a place, and having performed peace and nourishment for all sentient beings with a virtuous mind, leave this place and go to another supreme abode—go, go, svāhā!
Thus is the ritual for dismissing the Earth Deity.

Then, one should perform the expulsion of Māra according to the previously mentioned procedure with these mantra syllables: OṂ ĀḤ HŪṂ HOḤ HAṂ KṢAḤ HRĀḤ HRĀḤ HRĀḤ HRĀḤ RA RA RA RA VAJRĀNALA-SARVĀVARAṆADHARMAPRALAYASVABHĀVA SARVAMĀRAKĀYIKAVIGHNAVINĀYAKĀDĪNĀM DAŚADIGGATĀNĀM KĀYAVĀKCITTĀNI DAHA DAHA PACA PACA BHASMĪKURU BHASMĪKURU HŪṂ HŪṂ PHAṬ. This is the ritual for the expulsion of Māra, [concerning] all phenomena.
O, Huṃ Ka!
It does not exist; and one should cause it to increase, O.
O venerable ones, [reflect upon] the phenomena of the village.
Bho Ga Ca Ho; Bho Rgyas Bho, Deśādhipatyā (Lord of the Land).
ca. in the heart; ga. and then cha. hūṃ; bho. hu~; ga. śyā'dhos.
And "bho" [is added]. Furthermore, "tataḥ" is added. Furthermore, "argha" is added.
ca. para ga. ca. bho. by means of samādhi; bho huṃ; bho huṃ hūṃ.
ga. phaṭ phaṭ cha. ho

In the *Vimalaprabhā*, regarding the consecration (*abhiṣeka*): "Then, having summoned the other obstructors, Vināyakas, and so forth, with the vajra-hook (*vajrāṅkuśa*), and bound them with the vajra-noose (*vajrapāśa*), one should visualize the wrathful king Vajrakīla—whose lower body from the navel downward is shaped like a spike—as plunged into the ten locations above the wicked ones. One should do this in five colors with these mantra-syllables: *oṃ āḥ hūṃ hoḥ haṃ kṣaḥ hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ phaṭ vajrakīlaka kāyavākcittajñānādhipate ṣaṇmukha ṣaḍbhuja ṣaṭcaraṇa sarvavighnavināyakādiduṣṭānāṃ kāyavākcittajñānāni kolaya kīlaya hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ*."

Then follows the mantra of the Vajra Hammer: *oṃ llaḥ vajramudgara mārādīnāṃ śirasi kaṇṭhe hṛdaye nābhau guhye'nte vajrakīlakān ākoṭaya ākoṭaya kṣaṃ kṣāṃ kṣi kṣīṃ kṣu kṣū kṣa kṣa kṣa kṣū hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ phaṭ*.
This is the procedure for the ritual of impaling with the stake.

Then, for the sake of protection, one should install the ten wrathful kings upon the stakes according to the previously mentioned procedure. Thereafter, having placed *hūṃ hūṃ* on the soles of the left and right feet and touched the soles with the five-pronged vajra mudrā, one should pace within the center of the maṇḍala upon the ground in the form of Kālacakra, using the *ālīḍha*, *pratyālīḍha*, and *samapada* stances.
In the east, having placed *yaṃ yāḥ* on the soles of the feet and touched them with the sword mudrā, one should pace with the maṇḍala steps.
In the south, having placed *raṃ rāḥ* and touched them with the jewel mudrā, one should pace with graceful steps (*lalitapada*).

In the west, having placed *laṃ* and *lāḥ*, and having touched [the ground] with the wheel-mudrā (*cakramudrā*), one should preside over it with the vajra-posture (*vajrāsana*) or with the Viśākha-steps.

In the north, having placed *vaṃ* and *vāḥ*, and having touched [the ground] with the lotus-mudrā (*padmamudrā*), and having presided over it with the lotus-posture (*padmāsana*), one should then dance with the Tāṇḍava-steps.

Then, having worshipped the maṇḍala ground with substances such as scents using the mantra-syllables beginning with "Vajragandha," one should invoke the vajra-ground according to the previously stated procedure.
The mantra syllables here are: Oṃ lāṃ ā hūṃ, vajrabhūmi tiṣṭha mā cala hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ, vajradhara ājñāpayati svāhā.
Then the mantra-practitioner should again perform the offering of water for the feet (argha) and so forth;
this is the procedure for the consecration of the ground.
PHCG: Then one should consecrate the vajra-vases.
The mantra syllables for this are: *oṃ haṃ hāṃ hiṃ hīṃ haṃ haṃ huṃ halaṃ haluṃ vajrapadmāmṛtaghaṭa suviśuddhadharmadhātusvabhāva sarvadharmān suviśuddhadharmadhātusvabhāvān kuru kuru svāhā*.
Having offered incense and other offerings, one should place the Victorious Vase (*vijayakalaśa*) in the center of the mandala. This is the consecration of the vases and so forth.
22. Then one should perform the consecration of the vajra-thread; the mantra syllables for this are: Oṃ āṃ īṃ ṝ ḷ vajrasūtra sarvadharmaikasvabhāva sarvadharmān ekākārasvabhāvān kuru kuru svāhā.
Having offered perfumes and other substances, one should place it upon the eastern ground.
The ritual for consecrating the thread;
thereafter, one performs the consecration of the vajra-powder.

The mantra syllables here are: oṃ aṃ iṃ ṛ uṃ laṃ suviśuddha-pañcaskandhasvabhāva pañcaskandhān suviśuddhadharmān ato ato ato ga. ca. bho. āḥ kha. āṃ tantra, ga. ca. bho. huṃ hūṃ talaṃ *caṅkramet* (one should walk) kha. cha. bhūmyāṃ. Herein is the ritual for the consecration (*adhivāsana-vidhi*). Then: ṝ. Therein [the reading] "pañcaskandhasvabhāva" is absent in the chapters of ga. ca. cha. [Mantra: *kuru kuru svāhā*. [This concludes] the Great Chapter on the Compendium of the Ground and Other Elements Preceded by the Protection Wheel, Chapter 37.
Having offered incense and other items, one should place the vessels for the colored powders (rajobhāṇḍa) on the western ground; this is the procedure for the consecration of the colored powders.
Then follows the consecration of the vajra.

Therein are these mantra words: Oṃ hūṃ, O Wrathful Vajra, whose nature is compassion for all sentient beings, whose nature is the singular bliss of all phenomena, make all phenomena have the nature of vajra-bliss, make them so, svāhā!
Having offered incense and other offerings, one should place [the vajra] on the right; this is the procedure for the consecration (adhivāsana) of the vajra.
Thereafter, one performs the consecration of the vajra-bell.
In that regard, the mantra syllables are: Oṃ ho vajraghaṇṭe sarvadharmaikaprajñādhvanisvabhāve sarvākāra sarvadharmaprabodhani sarvadharmān niḥsvabhāvān prabodhaya prabodhaya svāhā.

Having offered incense and other offerings, one should establish [the implements] upon the northern ground; this is the procedure for the consecration (*adhivāsana*) of the vajra and bell. This concludes the procedure for the collection of the ground and other materials.

Then follows the consecration of the disciples: at the beginning, during the time of requesting the mandala; in the middle, during the collection of the ground and other materials; and at the end, during the time of entering the mandala—in all these instances, having prepared the mandala and given the tooth-stick (*dantakāṣṭha*), one then performs the protection (*rakṣā*).

In this regard, the procedure is as follows: for one who has bathed and put on clean clothes, having constructed a maṇḍala on that very ground in accordance with rites such as those for pacification (*śānti*), one should—having adorned the head with a garland of flowers and [anointed it] with perfumes and so forth—offer a tooth-stick (*dantakāṣṭha*) made of *udumbara* wood, twelve finger-breadths long, or from another milky sap tree, to one facing east, with this mantra: OṂ ĀḤ HŪṂ HOḤ HAṂ KṢAḤ VAJRADANTAKĀṢṬHA CATURVIMOKṢAMUKHAVIŚUDDHASVABHĀVA KĀYAVĀKCITTAJÑĀNAMUKHA VIŚODHAYA VIŚODHAYA SVĀHĀ.
Having thus given the tooth-stick, one should observe where it falls when thrown upward during the final consecration (*adhivāsana*) into the mandala;
whichever head it falls upon, the expansion of ritual activities (*karmaprasara*) and so forth pertaining to that [direction] will be accomplished for him.
This is the procedure for the tooth-stick.

14. Then, having led the disciple into the mandala ground, one should perform the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) of the six families—*oṃ āḥ hūṃ hoḥ haṃ kṣaḥ*—upon the head, throat, heart, navel, crown protuberance (*uṣṇīṣa*), and secret place. One should then impel Vajrasattva with these mantra words: *oṃ a ā aṃ aḥ vajrasattva mahāsukhavastra kālacakra, be present before the disciple; be well-pleased; be a granter of boons; perform, perform the consecration of body, speech, and mind, svāhā!* This is the procedure for the preliminary consecration (*adhivāsana*) of the disciple.

Then, having dismissed the disciple, the Master, having determined the divisions of the doors, places the Victorious Vase (vijayakalaśa) in the center of the mandala, the vajra-thread in the east, the vessels for vajra-powder in the west, the vajra in the south, and the bell in the north.

Having placed those [five items] in their five locations, he performs the consecration of the bed (śayyādhivāsana) in the south for the sake of determining auspicious and inauspicious signs, with this mantra: "Oṃ hoḥ! O bed, whose interior is the heart of the vajra-lotus petal, I perform the great sleep of vajra-bliss, just as it was performed by the Tathāgata; haḥ haḥ svāhā!
Thus is the consecration of the bed.
Then the teacher prepares his bed with the head toward the west and the feet toward the east;
with that, *cha ho*. There is no latent impression (*vāsanā*) in any form; on the ground, *huṃ ho*, there is no latent impression; in the five, *cha* is the latent impression.

O Vimalaprabhā, if one perceives a sign there through the power of meditation or in a dream— whether seeing the hosts of Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and goddesses with lutes and other symbols in their hands, that is auspicious;

or if one sees Vajra-Ḍākinīs with *kartī* and *kapāla* in their hands, or the Lords of Wrath (*krodhendras*) destroying Māras, obstacles, Vināyakas, and so forth, up to the edge of the protection wheel (*rakṣācakra*), even then it is auspicious.
Then, if he sees nothing at all, that is middling.

If, however, the master or the disciple should see beings belonging to the host of Māra—whose bodies are emaciated, parched, and withered by hunger and thirst, who hold knives and skull-cups in their hands, and who delight in harming virtuous people—that is an ill omen.

Upon seeing this, the Vajrācārya should leave his bed and, on the ground to the east of the maṇḍala, visualize the previously described protection wheel; then, according to the previously stated procedure, he should again offer them a very magnificent bali-offering.
Furthermore, the purification mantra is: *oṃ phreṃ vajraḍākinī vajradhātvīśvarī gaganasvabhāvasarvadravyaviśodhani sarvadravyāṇi viśodhaya hūṃ phreṃ phaṭ*.
This is the mantra for purifying the *bali* offering.
Then, for the pacification of obstacles, one should invoke the Buddhas: "May the Buddhas come—the Fathers together with the Mothers, along with their sons, servants, friends, and kinsmen."
The hosts of celestial deities, gathered together in their entirety, were gratifying the excellent Vajrasattva.

By means of this verse, one should place the Tathāgatas and others within one's own body, each in their respective element; such is the procedure for the invocation of the Buddhas. Thereafter, one should summon Vajraḍākinī.

The mantra syllables for that are: *oṃ ha hā hi hī vajrabhairava ākarṣaya ākarṣaya praveśaya praveśaya bandhaya bandhaya toṣaya toṣaya jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ vajraḍākinīnāṃ hṛdayaṃ hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ phaṭ*. This is the mantra of summoning.

Then, having offered the *bali* for the Vajraḍākinīs—accompanied by perfumes, flowers, incense, lamps, and unbroken rice (*akṣata*)—by means of the Vajramudrā according to the previously mentioned procedure while uttering "Phreṃ," one should visualize them consuming food and drink upon the grounds of the external cremation grounds; this is the mantra for summoning the Ḍākinīs.

Then, for the sake of pacifying the disturbances caused by the obstacles of Māra, one should first perform the protection wheel (*rakṣācakra*), adopt the yoga of Vajrabhairava, and apply the six-limbed mantra-installation (*ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*) according to the ritual of accomplishment. Having unified the gnosis-being (*jñānasattva*) with the commitment-being (*samayasattva*) through the procedure taught in the sādhana, one should visualize the deity as described below: possessing twenty-six arms, twelve eyes, six shoulders, four faces, three necks, and two bellies, bearing the weapons to be described. Then, having installed the previously mentioned seed-syllables within one’s own body, one should thereafter request empowerment.

Therein are the mantra syllables: Oṃ haṃ hāṃ hiṃ hīṃ haṃ haṃ huṃ hūṃ haṃ lahaṃ la ā ī ṝ ū lṛ vajraḍākinyo vajrāmṛtaghaṭair abhiṣiñcantu māṃ svāhā | Oṃ oṃ iṃ ṝ uṃ laṃ sarvabuddhā vajramukuṭaṃ mama pañcabuddhātmakaṃ bandhayantu huṃ hūṃ phaṭ | Oṃ a ā oṃ aḥ ha hā haṃ ha phra hoḥ sarvapāramitā mama vastrapaṭṭaṃ bandhayantu huṃ hūṃ phaṭ.

Oṃ hūṃ hoḥ! O Vajra and Vajra-bell, whose nature is consciousness and primordial wisdom, whose essence is compassion and insight, may Vajrasattva together with his consort bestow you upon my right and left hands. Hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ!

Oṃ ha hā yayā ra rā va vā la lā! May all the Kings of Wrath, together with their consorts, grant me the name "Vajra-pūrvaṅgama," whose nature is the equality of all—loving-kindness, compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity—huṃ hūṃ phaṭ!
Oṃ vaṃ! May the Lords of the Maṇḍala, Prajñā and Upāya, marked by the lotus and the vajra, grant me the limb of vajra-bliss-wisdom, haṃ haḥ hūṃ phaṭ!
Having thus made this supplication, one should then visualize oneself as having been consecrated by the seven empowerments.

Then, having received the seven empowerments, one should cultivate the sense of "I": "Oṃ, I have attained the seven stages through the seven empowerments of all the Tathāgatas. This is the procedure for the authorization of the seven empowerments.

Then, the mantra-practitioner should request the higher empowerment, such as that of the vase and so forth, with these mantra words: "Oṃ oṃ, may Wisdom and Means grant me the vase empowerment, huṃ hūṃ phaṭ!"
Oṃ āḥ! May Wisdom and Means grant me the secret empowerment, huṃ hūṃ phaṭ!
Oṃ huṃ! May Wisdom and Means, Vajrasattva and Viśvamātā, grant me the wisdom-knowledge empowerment, huṃ hūṃ phaṭ!
Having thus supplicated, one should then visualize oneself as having been empowered according to the procedure to be described.
Then one should cultivate the conceit [of identity]:
"Oṃ Oṃ! Having been consecrated by Vajrasattva with the Vajra-vase consecration, I am the son of Vajrasattva, having attained the stage (bhūmi) of Acalā.
"Oṃ Āḥ! Having been consecrated by Vajrasattva with the secret consecration, I am the crown prince of Vajrasattva, having attained the ninth stage."

One should cultivate the pride [of thinking]: "Oṃ hūṃ! I have been consecrated by Vajrasattva with the wisdom of insight; I am the second Vajradhara; I have attained the stage (bhūmi) of Dharmameghā. This is the procedure for the higher consecration (*uttarābhiṣeka*). Then, one should request the fourth consecration, which is higher than the higher, through the following mantra of supplication: "Oṃ ho! O Vajrasattva, whose nature is insight and means, grant me the consecration of the great mudrā-wisdom! Oṃ āḥ hūṃ ho phaṭ! Thereafter, one should visualize oneself as having been consecrated with stainless purity.
Then one should maintain the pride of Vajrasattva:

"Oṃ Hoḥ! By means of the fourth consecration of the syllable of the Dharmadhātu, I am consecrated as Vajrasattva himself; I am the second [Vajrasattva], who has attained the twelfth stage (bhūmi), the Vajrasattva of great purpose, the supreme immutable, the conqueror of the three worlds, the Blessed One Kālacakra, the letter EṂ. This is the procedure for the successive higher consecrations.
Now, the mantra syllables for the six mudrās: Oṃ haṃ haḥ, vajrakuṇḍale (vajra earrings) at the left and right ears, huṃ hūṃ phaṭ.
Oṃ aṃ aḥ, vajramekhalā (vajra girdle) at the waist and vajrakaṇṭhikā (vajra necklace) at the throat, huṃ hūṃ phaṭ.
Oṃ a ā, vajrarucakau (vajra bracelets) at the left and right hands, huṃ hūṃ phaṭ.
Oṃ ha hā, on the left and right feet, vajra anklets, hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ.
Oṃ haiṃ vaṃ, O Great Vajra whose nature is the five-syllabled great emptiness, crest-jewel, on the head; ashes on all limbs, hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ.
Oṃ oṃ, Ardhanārīśvara, vajra half-moon vajra-belt, hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ.
Oṃ a aḥ aṃ, O you who possess the single vajra-sound and the nature of the three sounds, upon whose shoulder is the vajra-sacrificial thread: huṃ hūṃ phaṭ.
Thus is the procedure for the six mudrās.

Then, the mantra-syllables for the elephant-hide (*gajacarma*): *oṃ kṣa kṣā kṣi kṣī kṣa kṣa kṣu kṣū kṣlṛ kṣlṝ kṣaṃ kṣaḥ hā hi hī hṛ ha hu hū hal hal haṃ haḥ sarvavighnavidāritagajacarma peṭārdraraktasravat phreṃ*. This is the procedure for the donning of the hide.
Then, one should place the ten serpent-kings (*nāgarāja*).

Therein are the mantra syllables: Oṃ hūṃ vajrajaya nāgendra vajrajaṭāmukuṭabandhe tiṣṭha tiṣṭha hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ | Oṃ kṣaṃ vajravijayanāgendra vajrapaṭṭabandhe tiṣṭha tiṣṭha hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ | Oṃ hyaṃ hyā vajrakarkoṭakavajrapadma vāmadakṣiṇakuṇḍalayostiṣṭha tiṣṭha hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ ||

Oṃ hrūṃ hlā, O Vajra-Takṣaka and Mahāpadma, stay, stay upon the anklets of the left and right feet! Huṃ hūṃ phaṭ!

Having thus performed the placement of all the mantras and mudrās, the practitioner of mantra (mantrī) should then recite the sixteen-line mantra of the *Ḍākinījāla* together with the mantra for subduing the wicked, for the purpose of subduing Māra and others; this is the rule.
Therein, the mantra words are as follows:
Namely: Oṃ! Homage to Vajrasattva;
homage to the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas; homage to the kings of the lords of the vajra-wrathful ones.
Homage to Viśvamātā! Homage to the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and Goddesses!
Homage to the Vajraḍākinīs!

Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One Kālacakra, who is terrifying as Vajrabhairava; whose body is the color of a great sapphire; whose white and red feet trample upon the hearts of Māras and afflictions; whose necks are black, red, and white; whose fierce, terrifying faces have fangs that are blue, white, yellow, and red; whose right and left shoulders are black, red, and white; who has twelve arms and twenty-six hands; whose hands hold a vajra, sword, trident, skull-bowl, bow, hook, hand-drum, mallet, discus, spear, staff, axe, vajra-bell, shield, khaṭvāṅga, skull-cup, bow, noose, jewel, lotus, conch, mirror, chain, the head of Brahmā, and an elephant hide; who is clothed in a tiger skin; who has a garland of severed heads hanging from his shoulder; who wears a vajra-band crown on his head and bears a vajra, a skull-cup garland, and a crescent moon; who is adorned with earrings, bracelets, a necklace, a girdle, anklets, ashes, a sacred thread, a crest-jewel, the Great Seal (Mahāmudrā), and the lords of serpents; whose heart is gladdened by the Ḍākinīs; whose feet are praised by Indra, Agni, Yama, Nairṛti, Varuṇa, Vāyu, Kubera, Īśāna, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Vināyaka, Kārttikeya, Nandin, Mahākāla, the planets, the constellations, the guardians of the fields, the lords of the gods, the lords of the asuras, the lords of the nāgas, the lords of the spirits, and the lords of men. This is the sixteen-word mantra of the Blessed One.
By ten million recitations of this [mantra], all rites are accomplished;
by one hundred thousand oblations, all eight great siddhis are attained—this is the rule for preliminary service (pūrvasevā).
Thereafter, it is recited.
By means of that alone, he performs everything;
now, those very same seed-syllables of the hundred families of Māras and the garland of skulls are also those of the *ḍākinī*-net.
Hṛ hā kṣa kṣā ṅa ṅā ka kā na nā ma mā ṇa ṇā tra trā huṃ hūṃ pheṃ phreṃ phaṭ phaṭ śmaśāne kla kla khu khū gṛ gṛ ghi ghī ha hā huṃ huṃ phaṭ— thus in the space wheel (ākāśacakra).
Clṛ clu chu chū nṛ nṛ jhi jhī ya yā huṃ hūṃ phaṭ— thus in the wind wheel (vāyucakra).
*ṭḷ ṭūla ṭhu ṭhū ḍḍa ḍḍū ḍhi ḍhī ra rā huṃ huṃ phaṭ*—thus in the fire wheel (*agnicakra*);
*pḷ plu phu phū bṛ bṛ bhi bhī va vā huṃ huṃ phaṭ*—thus in the water wheel (*udakacakra*);
*tu tu thu thū dṛdṛdhi dhī lalā huṃ huṃ phaṭ*—thus in the earth wheel (*pṛthivīcakra*).

*Slū slū yu yū ṣū ṣū śiśī haṃ haḥ huṃ huṃ phaṭ*. In the Jñānacakra, these [mantras] correspond respectively to the vajra, sword, jewel, lotus, wheel, and knife; the goddesses of the days of the week are [placed] with the twelve seed-syllables beginning with *ha*.
*Ha hā hi hī hṛha huhū halūhalū haṃ haḥ*: thus, in the two hands of Wisdom and Means.
The remaining eight potsherds belong to the goddesses; [the syllables] *a ā aṃ aḥ ha hā haṃ haḥ pha hoḥ* are the ten perfections (*daśapāramitā*) and the mantra-words of the *Ḍākinījāla*.
This mantra is to be recited in the fifth chapter; this is the rule for the raudra-karma (fierce rite).
Now, the garland-mantra (mālāmantra) of the Blessed One is explained limb by limb.

Oṃ āḥ hūṃ ho haṃ kṣaḥ ha! Kṣa-ma-l-v-rya Kālacakra, tamer of the difficult to tame, ender of birth, old age, and death, conqueror of the three worlds, great lord of heroes, Vajrabhairava, vajra-body, vajra-limbs, vajra-eyes, vajra-ears, vajra-nose, vajra-tongue, vajra-teeth, vajra-claws, vajra-hair, vajra-pores, cloth-adorned, vajra-laughter, vajra-song, vajra-dance, vajra-weapon-handed, vajra-lord of wrathful ones, vajra-ḍāka, surrounded by the net of vajra-ḍākinīs, come quickly, come! By the command of Vajrasattva: all Māras, obstacles, Vināyakas, Kiṃnaras, Kiṃpuruṣas, Garuḍas, Gandharvas, Yakṣas, Rākṣasas, Bhūtas, Mahāpretas, Kūṣmāṇḍas, Apasmāras, Kṣetrapālas, Vetāḍas, Pūtanas, wicked Nāgas, Grahas, and so forth; all fevers, all diseases, and those who cause minor calamities; all who delight in doing harm to all sentient beings—draw them all in with the vajra-hook, *jaḥ*, quickly! Having drawn in those gone to the upper direction, having drawn in those gone to the eastern direction, having drawn in those gone to the southern direction, having drawn in those gone to the northern direction, having drawn in those gone to the western direction, having drawn in those gone to the north-western direction, having drawn in those gone to the north-eastern direction, having drawn in those gone to the south-western direction, having drawn in those gone to the south-eastern direction, having drawn in those gone to the lower direction, having drawn in those gone to the sphere of space, having drawn in those gone to the sphere of wind, having drawn in those gone to the sphere of fire, having drawn in those gone to the sphere of water, having drawn in those gone to the sphere of earth, having drawn in those gone to the desire realm, having drawn in those gone to the form realm, having drawn in those gone to the formless realm, having drawn in those gone to the element of speech, having drawn in those gone to the element of mind, having drawn in those gone to the five aggregates, having drawn in those gone to the five elements, having drawn in those gone to the five sense-faculties, having drawn in those gone to the five objects of sense, having drawn in those gone to the five organs of action, having drawn in those gone to the objects of the five organs of action, having drawn in those gone anywhere from every direction—cast them down upon the ground blazing with vajra-fire in the great cremation ground! Bind them with the vajra-noose in all their arms! Restrict them with the vajra-chain in all their feet! Those who delight in causing affliction to the body, speech, and mind of all sentient beings—pulverize them with the great wrathful vajra! Cut them apart with the vajra-sword! Pierce them with the vajra-trident! Strike them with the vajra-knife! Pierce them with the vajra-arrow! Stake them with vajra-stakes! Pound them with the vajra-mallet! Slice them with the vajra-wheel! Split them with the vajra-lance! With the vajra-staff, having drawn in those gone to the body-element... [in the chapter, verse]... draw them in, draw them in! *(Note: The text provided ends mid-sentence regarding the "paṭala" and "śloka".)*

The Great Chapter on the Collection of the Grounds and Other Elements Preceded by the Protection Wheel: *Taḍaya taḍaya!* Strike, strike! *Chinna chinda!* Cut, cut! Having divided [the enemy] into three and a half million pieces, offer an oblation (*bali*) to all the spirits (*bhūta*) upon the ground of the cremation ground! With the vajra-hand-drum (*vajraḍamaruka*), having summoned the Vajra-Ḍākinīs, present the blood of the hosts of Māras to the Vajra-Ḍākinīs; present the five nectars (*pañcāmṛta*) to those who carry the five nectars! Together with all the Vajra-Ḍākinīs, perform pacification (*śāntika*), enrichment (*pauṣṭika*), protection (*rakṣā*), defense (*varaṇa*), and concealment (*gupti*) for all sentient beings! *Hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ!* This is the *pratyaṅga-mālā-mantra* of the Blessed One, Vajrabhairava-Kālacakra. By reciting it seven times over all malevolent ones—the lords of all Māras, obstacles, invincible pretas, and so forth—it effects their subjugation.

For this [mantra] as well, one must first perform a recitation (*jāpa*) of ten million and an oblation (*homa*) of one million for each ritual act; the rule is that there should be a recitation of one million and an oblation of one hundred thousand.
Then, having performed the suppression of Māra, one should repeatedly prepare the bed and seat until one obtains an auspicious sign.
Then, leaving the bed and taking up the vajra and vajra-bell, one should once again offer the bali.

Then, on the western ground of the mandala, facing east, one should worship the vajra-thread with perfumes, incense, and so forth. Thereafter, having mixed together sandalwood (*śrīkhaṇḍa*), rice-flour (*śālipiṣṭa*), blood, poison, charcoal from a funeral pyre, saffron (*kuṅkuma*), red sandalwood, turmeric (*haridrā*), and water with *tālaka*—according to the intention for rites such as pacification (*śānti*) and so on—the preceptor, holding the thread with his left fist, and the disciple, facing west and holding the thread with his right fist, should stretch it out between the western and eastern grounds and recite this mantra: OṂ ĀḤ HŪṂ A! All phenomena are of one nature in body, speech, and mind; I am Vajrasattva in a single form. I mark the vajra-ground with the thread. HŪṂ ĀḤ PHAṬ.
Then one should recite the mantra for the vajra-thread:
*oṃ vajrasūtraikākārasvarūpeṇa jaḥ jaḥ jaḥ sarvadharmān sūtraya oṃ āḥ hūṃ ho haṃ kṣaḥ phaṭ*.

With the left leg in the half-lotus posture (*vāmārddhaparyaṅka*) and the right foot resting on the ground, the disciple—with the right leg in the full lotus posture (*dakṣiṇaparyaṅka*) and the left foot resting on the ground—should cast the Brahma-thread from east to west.

Then the preceptor stands on the southern ground and the disciple stands on the northern ground; they cast the north-south Brahma-thread passing through the four gates to the tops of the stakes at the east, west, south, and north. Then, according to their own preference, they should drop the diagonal thread. Again, by that same method beginning with the cross-legged posture (paryaṅka), they should drop the thread from the northwest to the southeast, and then from the southwest to the northeast. Then, avoiding the "barrier of the directions" (diśāparigha), starting from the east-west Brahma-thread, they should drop a thread upon the southern ground.
Then, on the northern ground; then from the southern-northern Brahma-thread on the western ground; then on the eastern ground;
having offered incense, perfumes, and so forth, one should protect the threads used for the mandala-work and erase all the remaining [lines].
Having purified all the doors, one should again offer incense, perfumes, and the bali-offering, and perform the recitation of mantras according to the previously stated procedure.

Thus ends the second great chapter, the Compendium of the Grounds and so forth preceded by the Protection Wheel, in the *Vimalaprabhā*, the twelve-thousand-verse commentary on the *Laghukālacakra-tantrarāja* that follows the *Mūlatantra*.
In the *Vimalaprabhā*, the Great Chapter entitled "The Drawing of the Maṇḍala":
Having prostrated to Kālacakra, the Great Bliss, the foremost of the three vajras and the leader of those belonging to the maṇḍala,
[in] the maṇḍala divided into thirty-two parts.

Having laid down the vajra-lines by means of portions of the digits of the moon and Venus, I shall further elaborate the characteristics of the mandala of body, speech, and mind according to the portions of the digits, following the Root Tantra,
as it was taught in detail by Mañjuvajrin in the *Laghutantra*.
For the sake of destroying the egoism of those sages who advocate birth [as a caste],
[this was taught] within the three glorious maṇḍalas according to the measurements of four cubits plus half a finger-breadth.

[Regarding the Consecration: Here, the characteristics of the mandala extracted from the *Paramādibuddha*—which was sung by Mañjuśrī beginning with the thirty-fifth verse—are now being elaborated in accordance with the *Mūlatantra*: "From the Brahma-thread, this thread of one hundred and sixty-eight [units] is to be applied for the division of the directions; according to the statement regarding half a finger-breadth, the mandala consists of eight times four [units] within the center of the womb.

Outside the womb, the entire great mandala is constructed up to the boundary of the gates; one should display the walls, the archways and so forth, and the circle of fire and wind upon the outer ground."

By the words "the sūtra," and so forth, it is here established that on the previous mandala ground, the Vajrācārya faces east while the disciple and the Karmavajrī face west; having measured out the square mandala ground, one should drop the Brahma-sūtra in the center.
Then, the Ācārya, facing north, stands to the south, and the disciple, facing south, stands to the north; they should drop the Brahma-sūtra—this is the rule for the Brahma-sūtra.
One should drop the diagonal thread for the sake of purifying the corners;
then, from the Brahma-thread, this thread of ninety-six [units] is to be applied toward the division of the directions.
Here, from the central Brahma-thread, in the southern direction, there are ninety-six [units].

Having laid down the threads—ninety-six in the north, ninety-six in the east, and ninety-six in the west—it is stated by the *sūtra* that "by the eight pairs" (*vasuyugaiḥ*) in the sense of being extensively [marked] by the threads.
The meaning is that within the center of the forty-eight-thread mandala of the womb (*garbha*), there is the mind-mandala (*cittamaṇḍala*).
Outside the womb, it is constructed with all [the threads], namely one hundred and ninety-two.
The great maṇḍala [is defined] as "up to the boundary of the gates";
by doubling the lines from the lines of the central maṇḍala, the speech maṇḍala is formed up to the boundary of the gates;
by doubling the lines from the lines of the speech maṇḍala, the body maṇḍala is formed up to the limit of the gates.

Then, on the body-maṇḍala, one should display five walls, a gateway, and the fourfold circle of earth and the other elements, as well as a row of cloths, on the outer ground—meaning on the ground of space.
This is the rule for laying out the lines (*sūtrapāta*), which has been explained with its full elaboration.
Then, with threads... [ka. kha. ga. cha.];
twenty-five [ka.]; thirty-six [bho.]; second [bho.]. [ga. contains the word "iti" additionally.
